title: PR #482 — notification fan-out
summary: Replaces the inline email send with a strategy-per-channel dispatcher behind a factory, and emits a domain event so the audit log stays decoupled.

nodes.label: notification.controller.ts
nodes.summary: The HTTP entry point. It used to build the email body and call MailerService itself; now it validates the request and hands the payload to the dispatcher, so the controller no longer knows which channels exist.
details: 21 removed lines are the inline template building, now gone from the controller.
Dispatcher arrives by constructor injection at line 29.

nodes.label: dispatcher.service.ts
nodes.summary: New file. Holds the channel registry, resolves one channel per request from the notification payload, runs it, then emits notification.sent so nothing downstream has to be called inline.
details: createChannel() at line 92 maps the channel name to a concrete strategy with a switch.
Emits notification.sent at line 71 after a successful send, inside the same try block.
No retry here: a failed channel throws and the controller maps it to a 502.

nodes.label: audit.listener.ts
nodes.summary: Rewritten to react to notification.sent instead of being called by the send path. Same audit rows written, but the write is no longer on the request's critical path.

nodes.label: mailer.service.ts
nodes.summary: Untouched; now called only from the email channel.
details: Untouched by this PR; only its caller changed.

nodes.label: NotificationDispatcher
nodes.summary: Holds the channel registry and resolves one per request.
details: Depends on the NotificationChannel interface only, never on EmailChannel or SmsChannel directly.

patterns.name: Strategy
patterns.intent: One interface per delivery channel so the dispatcher does not branch on channel type.

evidence.explanation: One method, one return type, no channel name anywhere in the signature. That is what lets the dispatcher stop knowing which provider it is talking to.
The three-branch if is gone. The dispatcher now asks for an implementation and calls it, so adding a fourth channel never touches this method.

patterns.name: Factory Method
patterns.intent: createChannel() maps a channel name to a concrete strategy.

evidence.explanation: The switch moved here and returns injected instances, not new ones. It picks a product and hands it back, which is the whole of Factory Method.

patterns.note: Medium: it is a plain switch, not a registry, so adding a channel still edits this function.

patterns.name: Observer
patterns.intent: Audit log reacts to a domain event instead of being called inline.

evidence.explanation: The send path emits after the channel returns. Nothing here knows who listens, so audit can be added or dropped without editing the dispatcher.
The other half of the pair. It subscribes by event name only, which is what makes this Observer and not a direct call.
